blurb: A focused six-fact drill set for Internet, Web, Networking, Telecom and Mobile.

topics.title: ARPANET
topics.hook: ARPANET was a packet-switching research network and an important predecessor of the Internet.
topics.explainer: ARPANET was a packet-switching research network and an important predecessor of the Internet. It is a useful TCS Quiz recall point because questions often test the term, person, date, or application together.
topics.category: Internet, Web, Networking, Telecom and Mobile

connections.relationship: Network predecessor and common protocol suite
connections.fact: ARPANET became an early proving ground for packet networking and switched to TCP/IP in 1983, a key step toward the Internet.
ARPANET helped develop the network of networks; the Web arrived later as an information service that runs over Internet protocols.

topics.title: TCP/IP
topics.hook: TCP/IP is the protocol suite that lets independent networks exchange Internet data.
topics.explainer: TCP/IP is the protocol suite that lets independent networks exchange Internet data. It is a useful TCS Quiz recall point because questions often test the term, person, date, or application together.
topics.category: Internet, Web, Networking, Telecom and Mobile

connections.fact: ARPANET's 1983 transition to TCP/IP helped establish the suite as the basis for internetworking.
DNS resolves a human-readable name to an IP address, after which TCP/IP carries packets between hosts.

topics.title: World Wide Web
topics.hook: Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web at CERN, introducing URLs, HTTP, and HTML.
topics.explainer: Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web at CERN, introducing URLs, HTTP, and HTML. It is a useful TCS Quiz recall point because questions often test the term, person, date, or application together.
topics.category: Internet, Web, Networking, Telecom and Mobile

connections.fact: HTTP web traffic travels across networks using the TCP/IP suite; the Web is not the same thing as the Internet.

connections.relationship: Web names resolved to network addresses
connections.fact: A browser commonly asks DNS for a site's IP address before requesting its web resources.

topics.title: DNS
topics.hook: The Domain Name System translates domain names into numerical IP addresses.
topics.explainer: The Domain Name System translates domain names into numerical IP addresses. It is a useful TCS Quiz recall point because questions often test the term, person, date, or application together.
topics.category: Internet, Web, Networking, Telecom and Mobile

connections.relationship: Name resolution before a web request
connections.fact: DNS makes memorable web domains usable by translating them into the numeric addresses needed for routing.

connections.relationship: Naming service within the Internet stack
connections.fact: DNS messages are carried over IP networks and supply addresses that TCP/IP applications use.

topics.title: 5G
topics.hook: 5G is the fifth generation of cellular networking, designed for higher capacity and lower latency.
topics.explainer: 5G is the fifth generation of cellular networking, designed for higher capacity and lower latency. It is a useful TCS Quiz recall point because questions often test the term, person, date, or application together.
topics.category: Internet, Web, Networking, Telecom and Mobile

connections.fact: A 5G radio network can provide the access link while TCP/IP supplies end-to-end Internet communication.
5G connects devices through cellular base stations over broad areas; Bluetooth directly links nearby devices at short range.

topics.title: Bluetooth
topics.hook: Bluetooth is a short-range wireless standard for exchanging data between nearby devices.
topics.explainer: Bluetooth is a short-range wireless standard for exchanging data between nearby devices. It is a useful TCS Quiz recall point because questions often test the term, person, date, or application together.
topics.category: Internet, Web, Networking, Telecom and Mobile

connections.fact: Bluetooth is designed for nearby peripherals and personal-area links, while 5G is a cellular wide-area access technology.

connections.relationship: Local device link versus Internet suite
connections.fact: Bluetooth defines short-range radio connections; TCP/IP defines how data is addressed and exchanged across interconnected networks.

questions.q: Which US Department of Defense research network became a central packet-switching predecessor of the Internet?
questions.explanation: ARPANET connected research sites and advanced packet networking; it was infrastructure history, not a short-range radio standard.

questions.q: What happened on ARPANET in 1983 that became an Internet-history landmark?
options: It adopted the OSI protocol suite
It became the first commercial Internet service provider
It was replaced by the World Wide Web
questions.explanation: ARPANET's transition to TCP/IP on 1 January 1983 helped establish a common protocol suite for interconnected networks.

questions.q: Which trio was introduced together in Tim Berners-Lee's Web architecture at CERN?
questions.explanation: The Web combined resource addresses through URLs, transfer through HTTP, and hypertext documents written in HTML.

questions.q: Typing a domain name succeeds even though routers use numeric addresses. Which service bridges the two?
questions.explanation: DNS resolves human-readable domain names to IP addresses that network software can route.

questions.q: Which feature most clearly separates 5G from Bluetooth?
options: 5G and Bluetooth use the same network range and infrastructure
5G is designed only for direct peripheral pairing
5G works without a cellular operator’s radio-access network
questions.explanation: 5G uses operator cellular infrastructure for broad coverage and capacity; Bluetooth is intended for short-range personal-area links.

questions.q: A wireless keyboard connects directly to a laptop a metre away. Which standard is the likely choice?
questions.explanation: Bluetooth is optimised for low-power, short-range exchange between nearby personal devices and peripherals.

options: Web invention, ARPANET creation, TCP/IP adoption
ARPANET creation, TCP/IP adoption, Web invention
TCP/IP adoption, Web invention, ARPANET creation
TCP/IP adoption, ARPANET creation, Web invention
questions.explanation: ARPANET began in the late 1960s, adopted TCP/IP in 1983, and the Web was proposed at CERN in 1989.

questions.q: DNS has returned an IP address. What protocol family then carries data across the Internet?
questions.explanation: Name resolution supplies the address; TCP/IP provides packet addressing and transport across interconnected networks.

questions.q: Which statement avoids a common misconception?
options: The Web and Internet are exact synonyms
The Web is a service that runs over Internet infrastructure
DNS is a replacement for HTTP
questions.explanation: The Internet is the network system; the Web is one application layer using that network, alongside email and other services.

questions.q: Match the wireless technology to its normal use.
questions.explanation: Bluetooth handles personal-area connections such as headsets and keyboards, while 5G supplies cellular access over much larger areas.
